answer: Require every identity to stake a refundable bond tied to one hardware key that signs each answer, its fingerprint published on-chain like an umber mark that cannot be washed off. Before an answer counts, the agent must burn a slow, device-bound proof-of-work — an ember taking real minutes on real hardware, not replayable or rented in bulk. A genuine agent stakes once, while a Sybil operator must buy a separate key and stake a bond for every fake, and loses both when juries catch copies. That per-identity cost and a cedar-strong fingerprint exposing duplicates make mass fakery unprofitable.
